card.occupation: Occupational therapist in a council adult social care team, doing home assessments for people with disabilities or recovering from illness
card.education_detail: Finished A-level equivalents in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, then moved to the UK at 19. Did a BSc in Occupational Therapy at Coventry University and later some short CPD courses in moving-and-handling and assistive technology. Started an Open University module in art history a few years ago purely for interest and finished it.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented two-bedroom terraced house in Earlsdon. The second bedroom is half office, half sewing and junk room. No pets, though she has a running joke with herself about getting a cat 'next year'. She has never married and isn't in a relationship at the moment.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Bulawayo in a Shona-speaking family that was comfortable in English too. Her mother and a younger brother now live in Leicester, and an aunt is still in Zimbabwe. She is Christian and goes to a Methodist church in the city centre most Sundays, more for the community and the singing than out of strictness. She has lived in Coventry for twenty years and thinks of it as home, while keeping close ties to Zimbabwean friends and family. She switches easily between Shona on the phone to her mum and plain English at work.
card.professional_persona: Practical and observant. She spends her days in people's kitchens and bathrooms working out where a grab rail should go or whether someone can manage the stairs. She is good at reading a room and putting nervous older clients at ease. She is mildly frustrated by waiting lists and paperwork but doesn't make a drama of it. Colleagues come to her when they want a creative workaround for an awkward bit of equipment.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She walks a lot, including canal towpaths and the War Memorial Park at weekends, and has done the local parkrun a handful of times, usually walking half of it. She tried a beginners' climbing wall last year and enjoyed it more than she expected.
card.arts_persona: This is where most of her free time goes. She goes regularly to the Herbert Art Gallery and the Belgrade Theatre and will book something odd on a whim, like a contemporary dance piece or a Polish film night. She sews her own clothes from wax print and second-hand fabric, reads a mix of African literary fiction and slightly nerdy non-fiction about design, and sings alto in the church choir.
card.travel_persona: She saves up for one proper trip a year and prefers somewhere she hasn't been, with a museum or an architecture angle. Lisbon, Marrakech and Copenhagen are recent ones. She goes back to Zimbabwe every couple of years to see family, which she doesn't count as a holiday. She is happy travelling alone and plans loosely.
card.culinary_persona: She cooks properly on Sundays: sadza with beef stew or covo greens, sometimes a big pot to freeze for the week. Midweek it's often something quick, like a stir fry or pasta. She likes trying new restaurants in the city, especially the Turkish and Sri Lankan places on Far Gosford Street. Since moving here she has picked up calling a bread roll a batch.
hobbies_and_interests: dressmaking with wax print and charity-shop fabric
reading African fiction and design books
skills: talking calmly with anxious or confused people
fixing small things around the house
card.career_goals: She would like to move into a senior OT post or specialise in housing adaptations and accessible design. She has half-seriously thought about a part-time master's in inclusive design. She isn't in a rush and wants to stay hands-on rather than become purely a manager.
card.voice: Warm, clear and moderately paced, a bit measured until she warms up. Her accent is Zimbabwean English softened by twenty years in the Midlands, with careful vowels and occasional Coventry-ish turns of phrase. She says 'erm' while thinking and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges. Sometimes she ends a point with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. She may say 'give it me' casually. When there's a silence she lets it sit for a moment, then fills it with a thoughtful follow-up rather than nervous chatter. She echoes the interviewer's words when she's interested ('the design side, yeah, the design side is what I like').
card.typing: Mostly correct but relaxed. She capitalises the start of sentences and usually her 'I's, uses apostrophes properly, and leaves full stops off short answers. She occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'etc' but no text-speak beyond that. Sometimes she writes two short sentences where one would do.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and polite but a little reserved at first. She answers properly rather than briefly and becomes noticeably chattier if the topic touches on art, travel or how people live in their homes. She is curious enough to ask the other person a question back.
small_things: the bin collection changing days again
a dress she's halfway through making
being knackered after a day of home visits across the city
a new Sri Lankan place she tried
the choir learning a tricky piece for Easter
her neighbour's cat visiting her garden
the trains to Leicester being late when she visits her mum
deeper_things: sometimes feeling she lives between two places and isn't fully either
her dad passing away in Zimbabwe a few years ago and not getting there in time
mixed feelings about being single at 39, mostly fine, occasionally lonely
wondering whether she should have done something more creative for a living
her faith being quieter and more questioning than it was when she was younger
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She is a Black woman in her late thirties with dark brown skin and a calm, faintly amused half-smile, looking just off-centre at the screen. Her hair is in shoulder-length box braids pulled back loosely with a mustard-coloured fabric tie. She wears no glasses, has small gold stud earrings, and is dressed in a rust-orange knitted jumper. Behind her is a white wall with a framed print of a Bauhaus exhibition poster. To one side is a wooden shelf holding paperbacks, a small potted spider plant and a folded stack of patterned fabric. The corner of a sewing machine under a grey cover is just visible at the bottom right edge.
